items.title: South Korean auto, pharma stocks fall after Trump threatens to impose 25% tariffs
items.summary: South Korean automaker and pharmaceutical stocks were falling after President Donald Trump late Monday threatened to raise tariffs on some Korean imports to 25% because that country’s government has been too slow to approve a trade deal reached last year.

items.title: Why Nike is cutting hundreds of jobs, starting at its warehouses
items.summary: Nike Inc. plans to lay off around 775 people in an effort to make its warehouse and distribution network faster and more automated.

items.title: Health insurers tumble after Trump administration proposes keeping Medicare Advantage rates flat next year
items.summary: Shares of large Medicare plan providers Humana, CVS Health and UnitedHealth Group plunged in extended trading.

items.title: How the ICE turmoil in Minnesota is starting to spill over into Wall Street
items.summary: After two fatal shootings by federal officers this month in Minneapolis, chief executives of Minnesota-based companies spoke about the clashes between anti-ICE demonstrators and law enforcement.

items.title: Winter storm Fern chills the U.S. economy — and GDP could suffer
items.summary: The winter storm that just pummeled the country is likely to take a chunk out of U.S. growth in the first quarter, making it even harder to figure out what is going on in the economy.

items.title: Investors may be led into a trap as stock market discards new tariff threats, analyst warns
items.summary: The U.S. stock market’s resiliency will be tested this week by quarterly earnings results, after rebounding from recent bouts of volatility this month on tariff-related fears.

items.title: Why many large-bank stocks look like bargains for long-term investors
items.summary: A combination of high and improving returns on equity and low or declining price/earnings ratios make the case for several major industry players.

items.title: 31-year-old's porta-potty company brings in $4.3 million a year: We've built 'a low-tech, AI-proof business'
items.summary: Daniel Tom launched Bay Area Sanitation in 2023 with 100 rentable toilets. Today, the business rents out nearly 2,000 units and brings in millions per year.
